inlines.text: Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei 关于我们首次公开募股的讲话：

blocks.text: 我和我的联合创始人创办 Anthropic，是因为我们相信，我们这个时代最强大的技术应当为全人类的利益而构建。

inlines.text: 我和我的联合创始人创办 Anthropic，是因为我们相信，我们这个时代最强大的技术应当为全人类的利益而构建。

blocks.text: Daniela 和我因一种疾病失去了父亲，而仅仅几年后，这种病就变得可以治愈了。我以生物学开启了我的职业生涯，希望能帮助未来的疗法更早到来。在实验室里，我看到了科学家们在试图理解疾病和开发新疗法时所面对的庞大而错综复杂的难题。

inlines.text: Daniela 和我因一种疾病失去了父亲，而仅仅几年后，这种病就变得可以治愈了。我以生物学开启了我的职业生涯，希望能帮助未来的疗法更早到来。在实验室里，我看到了科学家们在试图理解疾病和开发新疗法时所面对的庞大而错综复杂的难题。

blocks.text: 许多能够穿透这片荆棘的科学工具——基因编辑、基因合成、用光控制脑细胞的工具——最初都只是纯粹的想法。换句话说，它们来自思考。来自智能。

inlines.text: 许多能够穿透这片荆棘的科学工具——基因编辑、基因合成、用光控制脑细胞的工具——最初都只是纯粹的想法。换句话说，它们来自思考。来自智能。

blocks.text: 人类智能已经让鼠疫、天花和小儿麻痹症在世界上大部分地区成为历史。但对其他疾病的进展对许多患者及其家人来说实在太慢了。从一个伟大的想法到一种疗法可能需要几十年：从最初发现 DNA 中一种奇怪重复模式，到首个使用 CRISPR 治疗疾病的疗法获批，花了很多年。

blocks.text: 自然界充满了这样的模式。但我们破译其中大多数的智能太少；科学家太少，时间也太少。现在我们可以构建这种智能。无论是蛋白质折叠、药物设计、癌症遗传学，还是临床试验管理，生物学和医学许多领域的科学家都发现，Claude 能帮助他们在短短几年前所需时间的一小部分内完成研究。我相信足够强大的 AI 与人类协同工作，可以将一个世纪的科学和医学进步压缩到十年。

blocks.text: 我不想操之过急。在现阶段，我们只有早期成果。实验和临床试验仍需时间。尽管它们涉及缓慢而笨重的过程，我相信这些过程可以被 AI 大幅加速。我们希望未来有更少的家庭仅仅因为几年之差而错过治愈的机会。

blocks.text: 医学只是一个特别生动的例子，但还有许多其他例子。我们的客户——世界上最有雄心的公司、非营利组织和个人——已经在应用我们构建的智能来刺激经济增长；帮助人们摆脱贫困；保护民主和自由社会；甚至让 DMV 这样的日常服务运转得更好。我们很自豪能与他们并肩工作。我对我们未来能共同做的事情极其乐观。

blocks.text: 与此同时，我们一直坦诚，这项技术存在非常真实的风险。这些风险包括个人或民族国家对技术的滥用、经济颠覆，以及失去对 AI 系统的控制。我们讨论这些风险，不是因为我们认为它们不可避免，而是因为我们认为它们可以避免。

inlines.text: 与此同时，我们一直坦诚，这项技术存在非常真实的风险。这些风险包括个人或民族国家对技术的滥用、经济颠覆，以及失去对 AI 系统的控制。我们讨论这些风险，不是因为我们认为它们不可避免，而是因为我们认为它们可以避免。

blocks.text: 避免它们取决于构建 AI 的人所做的选择。如果我们对安全漠不关心，与如果我们痴迷于安全，AI 的发展将会有天壤之别。而对安全和公共利益的执着，从一开始就编织进了 Anthropic 的 DNA。从针对生物和网络风险的防护措施，到对齐训练和测试，再到像 X 光一样透视我们的模型内部，Anthropic 开创了理解和引导 AI 系统行为的方法。

blocks.text: 还有很多工作要做，最困难的安全工作还在前面。公司令人难以置信的人才使我们能够构建最有能力的 AI 系统，这些人才需要被引导——甚至比以往更加如此——去反复、再三检查这些 AI 系统是安全可靠的。

blocks.text: Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

inlines.text: Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

blocks.text: My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

inlines.text: My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

blocks.text: Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

inlines.text: Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

blocks.text: So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

inlines.text: So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

blocks.text: Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

blocks.text: Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

blocks.text: I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

blocks.text: Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

blocks.text: At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

inlines.text: At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

blocks.text: Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

blocks.text: There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

blocks.text: And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

blocks.text: If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.
